newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma passes budget code in first reading.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma passes budget code in first reading.

text.p: The Russian Duma lower chamber of parliament preliminarily approved on Friday a code governing how Russia's annual budget should be drawn up and implemented.

The draft budget code, which was passed in a first reading and will be amended and voted on again in September, would limit government budget cuts, currently a source of tension between the government and the Duma, to 10 percent of total spending.
The Finance Minister would approve cuts of up to five percent, while the government would have to approve cuts of five to 10 percent.
The draft code would also bow to Finance Ministry wishes and not separate its functions from that of the Federal Treasury.

Budget formation and execution is currently government by several laws and the 1998 budget, which a Finance Ministry official recently said would be submitted to parliament at the end of August, may be passed without the budget code.
The government and the Duma are currently working on a plan to cut 1997 budget spending by up to a fifth due to desperately low tax collection rates so far this year.

The 1997 budget stipulates that the government must submit revised spending plans to parliament if revenues fall below 90 percent of targeted levels. Budget revenues were 65 percent in the first four months of the year.
